title: Crossover shift log & action ledger — 2026-10-08
content:
Shift window: 2026-10-08 22:00 UTC -> 2026-10-09 06:00 UTC
Owners: Maya R. Singh (primary), Ethan Brooks (backup)
Summary (one-liner): Overall steady; two small P1-ish pageouts tied to cache invalidation and a transient autoscaler regression. Both mitigated; follow-ups created.

Incidents and timeline:
1) Incident SRE-2142 — Cache spike -> user-facing 5xx increase (severity: S2 moving to S1 briefly)
   - First alert: 2026-10-08 23:12 UTC (5xx ratio > 3% for 5m on hosted-api-prod)
   - Triage notes: On-call observed a surge in prefix-miss rate for KV cache across nodes in us-west-2. Requests began hitting quantized-variant fallback which caused higher latency and some downstream timeouts.
   - Immediate mitigation: Rolled back recent cache-control config pushed at 23:05 (reverted TTL change from 3s -> 1s). Manually flushed hot-key entries on 2 nodes to restore steady-state.
   - Commands used: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/cachectl flush --node=node-87; kubectl rollout restart deployment/cache-router -n us-west-2-prod
   - Outcome: 5xx rate normalized by 23:30 UTC; latency back within SLO.
   - Follow-ups: SRE-2142 assigned to Priya K. for RCA (root cause: config rollout ordering race). Tasks: add safe-deploy gating for cache-control changes; add metric for prefix-miss delta; add automated rollback on TTL deltas > 50%.

2) Incident SRE-2144 — Autoscaler jitter causing capacity thrash (severity: S2)
   - First alert: 2026-10-09 01:45 UTC (cpu utilization oscillation + repeated pod restarts)
   - Triage: Horizontal pod autoscaler (custom HPA v2) reacted to spike in tokenization microservice latencies after a heavy batch request from a partner test harness. Autoscaler cooldown misconfigured (30s) causing repeated scale-ins/outs.
   - Mitigation: Increased cooldown to 5m for autoscaler policy and applied temporary rate-limit to the partner test harness via IP ACL in ingress. Restarted affected node pools to clear transient state.
   - Outcome: Stabilized by 02:15 UTC.
   - Follow-ups: SRE-2144 assigned to Luis H. to add autoscaler integration tests and enhance SLOs for tokenization service. Add canary for partner traffic with synthetic load.

Operational notes and quick wins:
- Observability: Trace sampling low on a few routes (trace-sample-rate=0.01). Increased to 0.05 for the next 24h to aid debugging; will revert in 48h unless otherwise noted (tracked in CONFLUENCE ticket).
- Runbook edit: Drafted a short note in the cache runbook about safe TTL rollouts and the need for node-level prewarming. File: CONFLUENCE: Runbook/cache-ttl-updates (linked). Add checklist item: confirm prefix-miss delta < 0.5% across 10m before rollout complete.
- Temporary workaround added to routing policy: if fallback-variant QPS > 1% for >3m then route new requests to stable-model-02 in the same region. This is a short-term guard until caching rollout gating is implemented.

Open action items (for next 72h):
- [A] Priya K. (due 2026-10-11): RCA doc + deployment checklist for cache-TTL changes. (SRE-2142)
- [B] Luis H. (due 2026-10-12): Autoscaler test harness + canary for tokenization service. (SRE-2144)
- [C] Ethan B. (due 2026-10-10): Temporary rate-limit automation for partner test harnesses (apply per-tenant ACL).
- [D] Maya (due 2026-10-13): Post-mortem prep template; capture metrics and attach traces for both incidents.

Notes for next shift / handover points:
- Watch metric: prefix-miss-rate and fallback-variant-QPS in us-west-2 (alert threshold adjusted tonight).
- Watch metric: HPA scale event frequency for tokenization-svc in eu-west-1 and us-west-2; if >3 scale events in 10m escalate to eng-sre lead.
- Be aware: temporary routing guard to stable-model-02 is active in us-west-2 until SRE-2142 work is merged.
- If you see repeated cache flushes from deployment job svc-deploy-prod, pause and escalate — we suspect the job might be retrying without backoff.

Runbook / playbook diffs to consider (short bullets):
- Add pre-deploy validation step for TTL changes that runs a simulated prefix-miss test against a canary cluster.
- Add an HPA cooldown default of 300s for services with stateful caches or heavy JVM warmup.
- Introduce a synthetic steady-state probe for tokenization endpoints that runs every 2m to detect freeze/latency early.

Pager and communication log:
- 23:12 UTC: Pager sent to oncall-shift (cache anomalies) — acknowledged 23:14 by Maya.
- 23:20 UTC: Slack #ops bridge opened; @infra lead looped in.
- 01:50 UTC: Pager for autoscaler jitter — acknowledged by Ethan at 01:52, Luis joined bridge at 01:56.
- 02:30 UTC: Incident declared "stabilized"; summary posted to #incidents and short note to exec-ops.

Misc (notes to self / incomplete):
- Need to check if the partner test harness was using an old SDK version; logs indicated repeated large batch sizes. Add to SRE-2144 investigation.
- Consider adding a nightly job to rotate cache hot-keys to avoid hotspots during peak test cycles.

Attachments / quick references:
- Recent deploys: github.com/redwood-inference/deployments/actions/2026-10-08-2300 (TTL change merged)
- Related runbooks: CONFLUENCE: Runbook/cache-basics, CONFLUENCE: Runbook/autoscaler-guidelines
- Jira: SRE-2142, SRE-2144

Closing note: Overall good response time from on-call team; mitigation patterns worked. We should prioritize gating for small config changes and add a short preflight that simulates cache-miss behavior. Leaving this log as the crossover ledger for the morning team — please ping me on Slack if anything degrades.

Signed-off-by: Maya R. Singh
